This device tracks the health of the Matter bridge node process itself (issue #286) — it does not represent a Matter accessory.

Choose which Indigo devices are exported to Apple Home and other ecosystems as Matter accessories. This bridge exports only what you add here; each Matter Bridge device is its own accessory with its own pairing code. Devices this plugin created itself, and device types Matter cannot represent faithfully, are listed with the reason they cannot be exported.
Type part of a device name, then click Apply filter. Leave empty to list everything.
Device:
Field.Description: A ● marks a device that is already exported.

Field.Label: Publish device:
Field.Description: Make this device available to Matter (untick + Add / update export to unpublish but keep its settings)

Field.Label: Device state:
Field.Description: This device's plugin keeps its reading in a state of its own rather than in Indigo's on/off flag, so tell the bridge which one it is.

Field.Label: Export as:
Field.Description: Indigo cannot tell a plug from a lamp or a lock, so you declare it. The first option is the safest default.

Field.Label: ⚠ Alexa cannot model water leak, freeze or rain sensors over Matter. If an Alexa/Echo is paired with this bridge, exporting this device stops state updates for EVERY exported device in Alexa — or Alexa may silently drop its own pairing (Apple Home is unaffected). Only export it if you don't pair Alexa.
Reading is inverted:
Field.Description: Tick if the device reports on/true for the OPPOSITE of what this role publishes. Contact sensors start ticked: Indigo reports a door as on when it is OPEN, while Matter reads it as closed.

Field.Label: ON / LOCK / OPEN runs:
Field.Description: Optional: an action group to run instead of the device's own command (needed when the device cannot do it itself, e.g. a sensor shown as a lock)

Field.Label: Optional, 2000-6535K. Declares the bulb's real warm/cool limits so paired ecosystems never ask for a colour it cannot reach — a starting point only: the plugin also learns this automatically from what the device actually does, and a measured side always takes priority over a typed value there. Clearing both removes what you typed; a side the plugin has already measured stays published at its measured value, not the generic range.
Optional. Leave empty to use the Indigo device name.
Invert position (0% = open):
Field.Description: Matter's convention is 100% = fully open. Tick this if your Indigo device is the other way round.

Field.Label: A robot vacuum is published as its OWN Matter accessory (Apple Home and Alexa cannot use one behind a bridge). After adding it here, pair it with Plugins ▸ Matter ▸ Pair Matter Vacuum… — pairing the bridge does not add it.
Status state:
Field.Description: Where the vacuum reports what it is doing (cleaning, docked, charging…).

Field.Label: Resume runs:
Field.Description: Leave as none to use the Start action group.

Field.Label: Play sound runs:
Field.Description: Apple Home's "Play sound to locate". Leave as none if your vacuum plugin has no find-me action.

Field.Label: Optional — rooms and cleaning modes. List the rooms as id=name using the vacuum's OWN room ids (from its app's map), e.g. 1=Kitchen, 7=Hallway. When you pick rooms or a mode in Apple Home, the room ids (e.g. 7,1 — empty means everywhere) are written to the variable below, then Start runs: have your Start action group pass them to your vacuum plugin. A cleaning mode runs its own action group (and/or is written to a variable).

Field.Description: Vacuum then mop (tick none for a vacuum that cannot mop)

Field.Label: Vacuum then mop runs:
Field.Description: Runs as soon as the mode is changed in Apple Home. Only ticked modes are used.

Field.Label: Pairing: opens a pairing window for THIS bridge and shows its QR code and setup code in a browser on the Indigo Mac (they are also written to the event log). Once the first ecosystem has paired, each further one needs a new window. The bridge only runs while it exports at least one device.
